author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새 수천 마리 · 겨울철새 수백 마리
habitat: 하천, 저수지, 논, 강의 얕은 물가

months.note: 봄과 가을에 지나가고 일부는 겨울을 나며, 6월에는 거의 보이지 않는다.

summary: 봄과 가을에 찾아오는 나그네새이며, 일부는 겨울에도 머무는 겨울철새이다. 하천, 저수지, 논, 강처럼 물이 얕은 물가에서 볼 수 있다. 쉬지 않고 움직이며 물 가장자리를 따라 진흙 속의 작은 무척추동물을 잡는다.

points.en: head and breast clearly streaked brown (breeding)
tail with two or three broad black bars

points.ko: 날 때 어두운 갈색으로 보이는 날개 아랫면

young: 어린새는 어른새와 비슷하나 날개덮깃과 셋째날개깃 가장자리의 작은 점이 흰색이 아니라 담황색이다.

similar.how: 깝작도요는 날 때 허리가 어둡고 흰 날개띠가 뚜렷하며, 가슴 양옆의 갈색 무늬 사이로 흰색이 접은 날개 앞까지 올라온다.

art.subject: Green Sandpiper (Tringa ochropus), adult in non-breeding plumage as seen at Korean streams and reservoirs in winter: head and neck dull grey-brown with very fine streaks; a short white supercilium only in front of the eye and a conspicuous complete white eye-ring; upperparts very dark olive-brown, almost blackish, with tiny buff-white spots along the feather edges; breast washed grey-brown with faint streaks, forming a dark band sharply cut off from the clean white belly and undertail; white rump; white tail with two or three broad black bars towards the tip. Bill dark greenish-grey, blacker towards the tip; dark eye; legs dull greyish-green.
art.pose: walking busily along the muddy edge of a stream, picking small invertebrates from the mud
art.scene: Korean shallow stream and reservoir edge with muddy margins in winter; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (April–May), side view standing: dark olive-brown upperparts densely dotted with small white spots, white fore-supercilium and white eye-ring, head and breast boldly streaked dark brown, streaked breast sharply divided from the white belly, greyish-green legs
adult winter plumage, side view standing: plainer dark olive-brown upperparts with tiny buff spots, faint streaks on head and breast, same white eye-ring and short white fore-supercilium
in flight seen from above: blackish wings without a wing-bar, square brilliant white rump, white tail with two or three broad black bars near the tip
in flight seen from below: very dark brown, almost blackish underwing contrasting with the white belly, barred white tail
art.build: Medium-small, stocky sandpiper, a little larger and plumper than Common Sandpiper and Wood Sandpiper; short neck, rounded head, horizontal stance, often bobbing the rear of the body. Bill straight, slender, slightly longer than the head. Legs fairly short for a Tringa, greyish-green. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight it looks strikingly black and white: blackish upperwing with no wing-bar, blackish underwing, a square, brilliant white rump and a white tail crossed by two or three broad black bars; only the toe tips project beyond the tail.
avoid: Do not give it pale or whitish underwings — that is Wood Sandpiper; the Green Sandpiper's underwing is blackish.
Do not extend a long white supercilium behind the eye; the white stops at the eye and the eye-ring is the main mark.
Do not paint bright yellow legs or a pale grey-brown back heavily spotted white (Wood Sandpiper).
Do not add a white wing-bar or a white wedge in front of the folded wing (Common Sandpiper).
